title: Dresden Christmas Markets Day Trip from Prague
short_description: See the Dresden Christmas markets in one day, with your own Mercedes and chauffeur. Door to door from your Prague address, time at the Striezelmarkt as the lights come on, and the same car back. Available from late November until Christmas.
description:
Every December the old town of Dresden turns into one large Christmas market. The Striezelmarkt on the Altmarkt has been held since 1434, which makes it one of the oldest Christmas markets in Germany. Around it are smaller markets with their own character, all within a short walk of each other.

This trip is only available in the market season, from the opening day at the end of November until shortly before Christmas. You can only choose dates inside that window when you book.

Your chauffeur collects you at your address in Prague at the time you choose and drives you north, over the border and down the Elbe valley. We suggest a late-morning start: you reach Dresden around midday, see the old town in daylight and are still at the markets when it gets dark and the lights come on, which is when they look their best.

You are dropped at the edge of the old town. From there the Striezelmarkt, the Frauenkirche and the Neumarkt, the Zwinger and the Semper Opera are all on foot. The car and the chauffeur wait for the time included in your booking, which is shown next to the price. If you want more time, add extra hours when you book.

The price is for the whole car, not per person. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls, parking and your time in Dresden. You see the total before you pay, and the same car and chauffeur bring you back to the door where the day began, with your shopping in the boot.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a guide. Market food, drinks, shopping and any tickets are paid by you on the day.
highlights: The Striezelmarkt on the Altmarkt, held since 1434, with its tall wooden Christmas pyramid
Dresden Christstollen, the city’s own Christmas cake, sold at the stalls where it is made
The Advent market on the Neumarkt in front of the Frauenkirche
The medieval Christmas market in the Stallhof courtyard, by torchlight after dark
The old town lit up after sunset, which comes early in December
Your shopping goes straight into the car, so you carry nothing back to Prague

itinerary.title: Pickup at your Prague address
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur meets you at the door of your hotel or apartment in Prague at the time you chose. If you asked for child seats, they are already fitted.

itinerary.title: Drive north to Saxony
itinerary.body: The route runs on the motorway through northern Bohemia, over the border and down into the Elbe valley. Both countries are in the Schengen area, so the border is normally just a sign by the road.

itinerary.title: Arrival at the old town
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur drops you at the edge of the old town and tells you where the car will wait. In the market season traffic in the centre is slow, so the drop-off point is chosen to save you time.

itinerary.title: The old town in daylight
itinerary.body: Walk to the Frauenkirche, through the Zwinger courtyard and past the Semper Opera while it is still light. The Advent market on the Neumarkt is right in front of the church.

itinerary.title: The Striezelmarkt
itinerary.body: Spend the afternoon at the Striezelmarkt on the Altmarkt: the Christmas pyramid, stalls of wooden toys and Ore Mountains crafts, mulled wine and Stollen.

itinerary.title: The markets after dark
itinerary.body: In December it is dark by late afternoon. Stay for the lights, then visit the medieval market in the Stallhof courtyard. Call or message your chauffeur when you are ready.

itinerary.title: Return to your Prague address
itinerary.body: The chauffeur collects you where you were dropped off and drives you back to the same address in Prague. Rest, warm up and sleep in the back.

includes: A private Mercedes with your own chauffeur, for your party only
Pickup and return at your address in Prague
The drive to Dresden and back
Waiting time at the destination for the hours included in your booking
Room in the boot for everything you buy at the markets
Child seats at no charge: tell us the children’s ages when you book
One price for the whole car, shown in full before you pay
excludes: Food, drinks and shopping at the markets
Entrance tickets, for example to the medieval market in the Stallhof or to museums
A guide or a guided tour: your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide
Extra hours beyond your booking, unless you add them when you book
pickup_info: Pickup and return are at your address in Prague: a hotel, an apartment or an office. Tell us the exact address when you book. Before the day you receive your chauffeur’s name and phone number, and on the day they wait at the door at the agreed time.
important_info:
This trip runs only in the Christmas market season. The Striezelmarkt opens in the late afternoon on its first day and closes early on Christmas Eve, so those days are not offered.

Carry a passport or national ID. Both countries are in the Schengen area and there is normally no check at the border, but police may ask for documents, and visitors from outside the EU need a valid passport and, where required, a Schengen visa.

Weekends in December are the busiest days at the markets. A weekday is calmer if your dates allow it.

Dress for the cold: you will be outdoors for several hours, and the evenings are often below freezing. Cards are accepted at many stalls, but carry some euros in cash, as smaller stalls often prefer it.

Many Dresden museums are closed on Mondays. Your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide.

faq.q: When can this trip be booked?
faq.a: Only in the Christmas market season, from the end of November until shortly before Christmas. The booking calendar shows only the dates inside that window. Outside the season, our regular Dresden day trip runs all year.

faq.q: What time should we leave Prague?
faq.a: A late-morning start works well. You see the old town in daylight and are still at the markets when the lights come on in the late afternoon. You choose the exact pickup time when you book.

faq.q: How is the price worked out?
faq.a: There is one price for the whole car, set for each car class. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls, parking and the hours in Dresden included in your booking. You can add extra hours when you book, and you see the total before you pay.

faq.q: What if we want to stay longer on the day?
faq.a: Tell your chauffeur. Time beyond your booking is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it, at the same extra-hour price you saw when you booked. Nothing is charged automatically.

faq.q: Can we leave our shopping in the car?
faq.a: Yes. The car waits for you during your booking, so you can drop bags with your chauffeur and walk on with free hands.

faq.q: Do we need passports for a day trip to Dresden?
faq.a: Yes, carry a passport or national ID. Both countries are in the Schengen area and there is normally no check at the border, but police may ask for documents.
